source: cargo run -q -p lp-emu-esp32c6 --release -- --elf target/emu-ref/735af98ae-boot-idle-memfs-usb/fw-esp32c6 --time-grade t2 --usb-sj file:target/validate/boot-idle.cap --usb-sj-tried file:target/validate/boot-idle.tried --usb-host attached --timeout 8s --wall-timeout 160 --strict-bus --exit-on '[stack] heartbeat: high-water' --efuse-mac a0:f2:62:87:b4:8c --efuse-rev 0.2
note: running the pinned image target/emu-ref/735af98ae-boot-idle-memfs-usb/fw-esp32c6 rather than building one. It is the shipped image over its own USB-Serial-JTAG link — no `spike_uart0_link`, no cherry-pick — so that it is the same bytes a silicon flash of the same commit puts on the board, which is what makes a memory comparison a comparison of two machines rather than of two link drivers (DD30). `scripts/emu/build-reference-image.sh esp32c6,server,radio,memory_fs <commit> none` builds it in a detached worktree at that commit.

trust.because: the same allocator and the same RAM model as t1, and the harness's 372 memory values are identical under both grades — a time grade must not move a heap byte. The one figure that does move is the idle stack high-water mark (11,432 B under t1, 11,752 B under t2), which is interleaving, not memory: the deepest interrupted call chain is not the same chain
t2 uses the per-class cycle model rather than one cycle per instruction, and no transcript grades it either. It is a rung up the ladder, not a promise about milliseconds on silicon
direct load prints no ROM or bootloader banner; the time grade changes nothing about that. M7 owns it
the same host-absent-only model as t1; M6 owns the attached and not-draining states
the same absence of pin observation as t1; M5 owns it
the same UART0 model as t1: the bytes are the guest's, a live socket's arrival times are the host's
